jobs.description:
Game communities are where players make friends, build worlds and create together. Most of the harm in them comes from a handful of users. Some are bullies who drive other players away. In a game built for kids, one of them can be an adult pretending to be twelve. Aiba builds the AI that finds them before a moderator has to, so the community stays a safe place to play and create. For studios, that means happier players, higher NPS and lower churn.

Our platform is called Amanda. It moderates chat, voice and images in real time, flags grooming, bullying and fake profiles, and gives moderators the tools to act fast. Teams at MoviestarPlanet, WildWorks and Rovio (Angry Birds) use it to keep their communities safe.

The timing is on our side. Rules like the DSA and COPPA have made online safety a requirement, not a nice-to-have. Game studios and social platforms now have to solve this, and they are coming to us to do it.

We are a small team in Oslo and Gjøvik. We need the person who turns that interest into customers.

The role in short
You own the deal from the first call to the signed contract, and the customer relationship after it. Marketing brings you the leads. You bring the curiosity, the pitch and the close. This is not a cold-calling job.

One week you're on a video call with the founder of an indie studio. The next you're in a meeting room with the compliance team of one of the big names in gaming. A few weeks later you're at a games conference, making deals over coffee with people from all walks of life.

What you'll do
• 
Run the full sales cycle: discovery, demo, proposal, negotiation and close.

• 
Sell to Heads of Trust & Safety, community directors and studio CEOs, from indie studios to the largest gaming companies.

• 
Shape Amanda around each community's problem. No two platforms have the same one.

• 
Own your pipeline and your numbers. ARR is the metric that matters most.

• 
Grow the customers you land. Many start with one problem and expand from there.

• 
Travel to gaming and online safety conferences roughly every other month to meet customers and close deals in person.

• 
Work closely with marketing, product and operations, and tell them what you hear from the market.

• 
Write the playbook. There isn't one. What you learn becomes how Aiba sells.

Who you are
• 
You have closed B2B software deals end to end for 3+ years.

• 
You close as comfortably on a video call as across a table.

• 
You build relationships as easily with suits as with gamers.

• 
You act before anyone asks. Low ego, high agency.

• 
You take feedback well, and you have a sense of humor. Both get used here.

• 
Your English is greatexcellent, spoken and written. More languages are a plus.

A bonus, not a must: startup or scale-up experience, a background in gaming or edtech, or knowledge of Trust & Safety.

Who this isn't for
If you want a finished playbook, a fixed territory and a manager who plans your week, you won't like it here.

What you get
• 
NOK 800,000+ base, plus commission paid quarterly. The more you close, the more you earn

• 
A place in the equity program for key employees

• 
Real impact. In a team this size, your deals visibly move the company.

• 
A fast track for your commercial career, in an industry that is growing fast

• 
A product you don't have to oversell. It keeps players safe, kids included.

• 
Conferences around the world, a passionate team, and the usual Norwegian basics: pension, paid holiday and parental leave

Apply on The Hub. It takes two minutes. First a short call with The Hub's team, then you meet the team at Aiba.

Our solution also leverages behavioral biometrics to track patterns of behavior, identifying repeat offenders and reducing harmful interactions over time.

Aiba.ai is scalable, supporting both indie games and large multiplayer platforms. Our APIs are customizable and easy to integrate into existing systems, allowing you to tailor moderation based on your needs. Additionally, our platform supports multiple languages, making it ideal for global games with diverse player bases. We provide real-time moderation across languages, ensuring all players are protected, regardless of location or language.

By offering advanced moderation and behavior detection, Aiba.ai helps developers create safer, more enjoyable player experiences. We reduce the burden on moderation teams, ensure regulatory compliance, and improve the health of gaming communities. Our commitment is to provide a robust, scalable solution that protects your players and helps foster a positive gaming environment.

• Strong electrical fault-finding skills and the ability to interpret single-line diagrams

• A secure, long-term position in a growing industry
• Training and development opportunities
• A safe, inclusive and supportive working environment

The Opportunity
Fossefall is building the infrastructure needed to power Europe's AI future. As our GPU and AI data centre projects move from design and procurement into construction, testing and operational readiness, we need a Commissioning Manager who can turn our commissioning strategy into a coordinated, evidence-based delivery plan.

Reporting to the VP Commissioning, you will lead owner-side project commissioning from design review and factory testing through installation verification, start-up, integrated systems testing and handover. You will connect engineering, construction, suppliers, Operations and IT delivery, identify gaps early and provide clear recommendations on readiness and acceptance. The role is based in Oslo with a hybrid working model and regular travel to project sites and supplier facilities.
What you'll do
• 
Develop and maintain the project Commissioning Plan, scope, schedule, resource plan and readiness gates, integrated with construction, utility availability and phased delivery.

• 
Review designs and supplier documentation for testability, maintainability and operational requirements.

• 
Coordinate the full L1-L5 commissioning process: factory testing, installation QA/QC and static tests, start-up and pre-functional checks, system or module SAT and integrated systems testing.

• 
Review and coordinate test method statements, scripts, load profiles, acceptance criteria, sequences of operation and cause-and-effect coverage with engineering SMEs, contractors, OEMs and the independent Commissioning Authority where appointed.

• 
Secure test prerequisites, including permanent or temporary power, load banks, thermal loads, cooling readiness, water quality, calibrated instruments, controls connectivity and safe working arrangements.

• 
Coordinate electrical, mechanical and liquid-cooling systems, BMS, EPMS and DCIM, fire and life safety, security and ICT/OT interfaces. Align facility readiness with rack, server, cluster and platform delivery leads.

• 
Use Omega365 as the system of record for commissioning scope, checklists, test evidence, digital sign-off, punch and NCR status, retests and readiness reporting.

• 
Manage commissioning risks, blockers, changes and deferred tests. Escalate failed acceptance criteria and readiness gaps with clear evidence and recommended actions.

• 
Prepare readiness recommendations, including RFC before L4, RFS following successful integrated systems testing and RFT after the agreed IT and service-validation scope.

• 
Coordinate Operations training, O&M deliverables, handover, the final commissioning report and the outstanding-item register.
About you
• 
Typically 5+ years of experience in commissioning or delivery of complex technical facilities, including responsibility for multidisciplinary commissioning.

• 
A Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Automation, Energy Systems or a related technical discipline. Equivalent practical experience from commissioning complex technical facilities may compensate for formal education.

• 
Strong working knowledge of power and cooling infrastructure, controls integration, functional testing, failure scenarios and integrated systems testing.

• 
Experience leading contractors, OEMs and specialist test teams through clear plans, responsibilities, decisions and escalation, including teams without a direct reporting line.

• 
The judgement to challenge test methods, assess evidence, manage cross-discipline interfaces and make clear recommendations on system readiness.

• 
A structured, pragmatic and decisive working style. You communicate technical risks clearly and follow issues through to verified closure.

• 
Fluent professional English, both written and spoken, and willingness to travel and work on site during critical testing periods.

• 
Experience from owner-side commissioning in data centres or other mission-critical environments, modular facilities, GPU or AI infrastructure, liquid cooling or first-of-kind systems would be valuable. So would experience with Omega365 or comparable digital commissioning tools, Norwegian or another Scandinavian language and a relevant commissioning or project management certification, but none of these is required.
What success looks like
Within the first few months, project commissioning is governed by a clear and trusted plan, testing is prepared before site execution and readiness decisions are supported by complete, traceable evidence. Engineering, construction, suppliers, Operations and IT delivery understand their responsibilities and interfaces. Risks are surfaced early, defects and deferred tests are controlled and handover is completed without avoidable gaps between facility readiness and technology deployment.
Why Fossefall?
This is an opportunity to shape owner-side commissioning capability while Fossefall's AI infrastructure portfolio is being built. You will work across the physical and digital layers of high-performance AI facilities, influence how projects move from construction into reliable operation and collaborate with specialists across engineering, project delivery, operations and technology.

We are still small enough for individual judgement and ownership to matter. You will have room to improve how we work, contribute to critical delivery decisions and help build repeatable commissioning practices for future projects.

Fossefall is a Nordic AI infrastructure company founded in 2025. We develop and operate AI factories powered by renewable energy, turning clean Nordic power into scalable, sovereign computing capacity for Europe, built in partnership with local communities, energy producers and technology leaders across the world. As a team, we are still small enough to know each other as people, and our culture is shaped by ownership, curiosity, warmth and collaboration.

jobs.description:
This is NTNU
NTNU is a broad-based university with a technical-scientific profile and a focus in professional education. The university is located in three cities with headquarters in Trondheim.

At NTNU, 8,6000 employees and 44,000 students work to create knowledge for a better world.

You will find more information about working at NTNU and the application process here.   
Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_KHQjc4ndas&t=41sAbout the position
We are looking for a highly motivated PhD candidate to join our research activities in reliability science for AI-enabled systems.

The PhD project will focus on developing methods to understand, assess, and improve the reliability and trustworthiness of AI-enabled systems. The research will address challenges arising when AI becomes an integral part of systems where failures or incorrect decisions may have significant operational, economic, environmental, or safety consequences.

The candidate will work in an interdisciplinary research environment combining reliability engineering, artificial intelligence, prognostics and health management, and industrial decision support. The position offers opportunities for collaboration with academic and industrial partners and for participation in international research activities.

Are you motivated to take a step towards a doctorate and open up exciting career opportunities? As a PhD Candidate with us, you will work to achieve your doctorate, and at the same time gain valuable experience that qualifies you for a further career in higher education and research, in and outside academia.

You will be supervised by Professor Janet Lin.
Duties of the position
• Complete the doctoral education until obtaining a doctorate
• Carry out research of good quality within the framework described above
• Academic publications and popular science dissemination
• Participate in the RAMS research group (RAMS - MTP - NTNU)
• Participate in international activities such as conferences and/or research stays at foreign educational institutions
• Collaborate with academic and industrial partners when relevant.
Be prepared for changes to your work duties after employment.
Required selection criteria
• You must meet the requirements for admission to the faculty's Doctoral Programme, see Section 6-1 of the PhD regulations for more information.
• You must have a relevant Master's degree in mechanical engineering, industrial engineering, computer science, or equivalent. Your degree must include a major independent project (minimum 30 ECTS) equivalent to a master’s thesis
• Master students can apply, but the master's degree must be obtained and documented before starting the position.
• You must have a strong and relevant academic background from your previous studies and have an average grade from your Master's degree study, or equivalent education, which is equal to B or better compared to NTNU's grading scale. If you do not have letter grades from previous studies, you must have an equally good academic foundation. If you have a weaker academic background, you may be considered if you can document that you are exceptionally suited for a PhD education, for example through relevant work experience and/or peer-reviewed academic works.
• You must have good written and oral English language and communication skills
• You must have a documented academic background in at least one area relevant, such as artificial intelligence, machine learning, reliability engineering, prognostics and health management, data analytics, automation and control, or related methods
The appointment is to be made in accordance with NTNUs guidelines for recruitment positions for general criteria for the position.
Preferred selection criteria
• Knowledge of or experience with artificial intelligence and machine learning methods.
• Knowledge of reliability engineering, prognostics and health management (PHM), condition monitoring, maintenance, or safety-critical systems.
• Experience with programming, data analysis, modelling, or simulation using relevant tools and languages.
• Experience with research-oriented work, for example through a Master's thesis, scientific publications, research projects, or other relevant research activities.
• Experience with industrial applications or interdisciplinary research involving engineering and artificial intelligence is an advantage.
• Knowledge of or interest in topics related to trustworthy AI, such as uncertainty, robustness, explainability, verification and validation, or AI safety, is an advantagePersonal characteristics
To complete a doctoral degree (PhD), it is important that you are able to: 

• Work independently and take responsibility for progressing your research
• Work in a structured way, set goals and make plans to achieve them
• Show curiosity, creativity, and strong motivation for the research area
• Analyze complex problems, assess different perspectives, and draw well-founded conclusions
• Communicate and collaborate effectively with researchers and other relevant partners
Emphasis will be placed on personal qualities.
We offer
• An exciting job with an important mission in society
• Developing tasks in a strong and international professional environment
• Career guidance and follow-up during the PhD period
• Open and inclusive working environment with committed colleagues
• Working capital that can be used to implement the project
• Mentor programme as a new employee at NTNU
• Favorable terms as a member of the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund (SPK)
• Free Norwegian language training at a basic level (A2)
As a PhD Candidate at NTNU, you will have access to employee benefits.
Diversity
Diversity is a strength, and at NTNU we aim to be an employer that reflects the diversity in society and that makes use of the potential of the population's collective skills. Our vision is Knowledge for a better world and our values ​​are creative, critical, constructive and respectful. We believe that an organization that is equal, diverse and gender-balanced is essential for us to achieve our goals. 

We strive to attract employees with different skills, life experiences and perspectives to contribute to even better problem solving of our societal mission in research and education. 

If you think this position is relevant and interesting, we encourage you to apply, regardless of gender, functional ability and cultural background, or whether you have been out of work for a period of time.

At NTNU we want to increase the proportion of women in scientific positions. We have a number of measures to promote equality.
Salary and conditions
In the position of PhD Candidate, code 1017, your gross salary will normally be NOK 580 000,- per annum depending on qualifications and seniority. A 2% statutory contribution to the State Pension Fund is deducted from the salary. 

The employment period is 3 years.

For employment as a PhD Candidate, it is a prerequisite that you gain admission to the PhD programme in Engineering within three months of your employment contract start date, and that you participate in an organized doctoral programme through out the period of employment.

As an employee at NTNU, it is important that you keep yourself up to date with academic and organizational changes and adapt to them.

For the necessary professional and social interaction, it is a prerequisite that you are physically present and available to the institution on a daily basis.

The appointment is carried out in accordance with the principles of the State Employees Act, and Export control (legislation that regulates the export of knowledge, technology and services). Candidates who, after assessment of the application and attachments, are considered to bein conflict with the criteria in the latter act, will not be able to be employed.
About the application
The attachments (including a description of your scientific work) must accompany the application as these documents form the basis of the application assessment. The documents must be in English.

Please note: the application will only be assessed on the basis of the information we have received by the application deadline. Therefore, make sure that your application clearly shows how your skills and experience meet the criteria described above. The application and all attachments must be sent electronically via Jobbnorge.no. If you are invited to an interview, you must bring certified copies of certificates and diplomas upon request.

The application must include:

• Transcripts and diplomas for Bachelor's and Master's degrees
• CV 
• Copy of Master's thesis. If you have recently submitted your Master's thesis, you can attach a draft of the thesis. Documentation of a completed Master's degree must be presented before taking up the position.
• Project outline containing proposals for an overall description of research questions, theoretical perspectives, methodological design for the project and progress plan (maximum 1500 words/4 pages) 
• Short letter of motivation (400 words/1 page)
• Possibly publications etc. other relevant research work
• Possibly certificates
• Names and contact information of three relevant referees
If all, or parts, of your education has been taken abroad, we also ask you to attach documentation of the scope and quality of your entire education, both Bachelor's and Master's education, in addition to other higher education. If your institution uses “diploma supplement” (normal for most European institutions), you must attach this. A description of the documentation required can also be found here. If you already have a statement from Norwegian Directorate for Higher Education and Skills (HK-dir), please attach this as well.

Joint work will be considered. If it is difficult to identify your contribution to joint work, you must attach a brief description of your participation.

When assessing the best qualified, we emphasize necessary qualifications such as education, experience and personal suitability. Motivation for the position, ambitions, and potential for research will also count when assessing the candidates.NTNU recognizes a wide range of academic contributions and has committed itself to The San Francisco Declaration on Research Assessment and CoARA (responsible assessment of research and recognition of a greater breadth of academic contributions in accordance with NTNU's social mission).
General information
A public list of applicants with name, age, job title and municipality of residence is prepared after the application deadline. If you wish to be exempt from entry on the public applicant list, this must be justified. Assessment will be made in accordance with current legislation. You will be notified if the exemption is not granted.

If you think this position looks interesting and in line with your qualifications, you are welcome to apply.

If you have any questions about the position, please contact Professor Janet Lin, e-mail: janet.lin@ntnu.no. 

If you have any questions about the recruitment process, please contact HR Senior Consultant Hedda Winnberg, e-mail: hedda.winnberg@ntnu.no.

Application deadline: 10.01.2027
